snippets: The Agent Builder MCP endpoint is generally available from Elastic 9.3 and in preview on 9.2. Outside Serverless, Elastic's subscription table lists MCP access under Enterprise. ... An API key works on every deployment and suits unattended agents. OAuth 2.1 works on Serverless only, and gives each person their own revocable connection. ... Tools run with the key's permissions. Restrict it to the indices the agent should read, and include the feature_agentBuilder.read Kibana privilege, which the endpoint requires.

Custom tools you define in Kibana reach the agent through the same endpoint. For a cluster older than 9.2, the deprecated standalone server still wraps _cat/indices, _mapping, _search and _cat/shards in four tools. It receives security fixes only. On Elastic 9.2 or later, use the Agent Builder endpoint. On older clusters, use the REST API or the standalone server, and plan the upgrade. The MCP endpoint is built into Kibana, so there is nothing to install.

It is <kibana-url>/api/agent_builder/mcp, or <kibana-url>/s/<space-name>/api/agent_builder/mcp in a custom space. Authenticate with an API key that carries the feature_agentBuilder.read Kibana privilege, sent as Authorization: ApiKey <key>. Serverless projects also accept OAuth 2.1. Claude Code speaks streamable HTTP, so it connects to the endpoint directly.

Tools run with the API key's privileges, and some built-in tools write. A broadly scoped key gives the agent that reach. ... Agent traces usually sit in a different product from the rest of your telemetry, so when a slow database makes an agent slow the symptom is in one tool and the cause is in another. Oodle keeps both in one query surface.See agent observability→ ... Yes. The Elastic Agent Builder MCP endpoint is built into Kibana at /api/agent_builder/mcp.
